_comment: BYS360 coverage ratchet baseline. Truthful, re-measured floor for CI's actual test scope (tests/quality -m "ci_safe" -- unchanged literal marker, now naturally selecting 40 more tests via per-file pytestmark -- then tests/integration tests/architecture tests/security tests/critical tests/services tests/migrations tests/workflow tests/release tests/communication tests/behavior tests/mobile + 33 loose tests/test_*.py files, branch=true). This value is NOT aspirational and must NEVER be raised automatically by any script -- raising it is a separate, human-reviewed action after real coverage genuinely improves. See scripts/quality/bys360_coverage_ratchet.py for enforcement logic and its docstring for the no-self-raise constraint.
_history: Phase 8 Top-Level Test Hygiene Closure (2026-07-27): tests/test_live_scope_and_security_static.py's pytest.mark.live/realdb/slow markers (withheld in Phase 7 pending review) were confirmed stale -- all 3 tests are plain Path.read_text() + string-presence checks, the markers predate this repo's earliest visible commit with no recorded rationale, and an identical mistagging pattern was found on another purely static file (tests/architecture/test_survey_live_contract.py, out of this wave's scope). Markers removed; the file added to the broad coverage-instrumented step (33rd of 33 loose tests/test_*.py files, all now included). tests/test_sp_routes_smoke.py's os.environ.setdefault calls were empirically proven to be inert no-ops (tests/conftest.py already sets the same 3 keys unconditionally at import time, before any test runs) -- confirmed via before/after and reversed-order probes showing byte-identical environment state; left unchanged (NO CHANGE -- NO ENVIRONMENT LEAK DEMONSTRATED). tests/test_feedback_pulse_privacy_behavior.py's ast.parse+exec() indirection (used to avoid importing app/services/feedback_service.py) was replaced with a plain import of the pure, side-effect-free target function -- verified to require no app-context/DB, behaviorally identical (2 isolated runs + both file orderings + post-full-suite re-run, all pass), and to raise its own coverage.py-attributed contribution from 0% (exec()'d code has co_filename='<string>', invisible to coverage.py) to a real, measurable contribution. Net effect: +3 tests (step2), 0 new/removed test count elsewhere in target files, +2 tests in tests/architecture/test_ci_coverage_scope_contract.py (contract updates: 2 obsolete blocked-file tests removed, 1 new marker-removal check added, existing TOP_LEVEL_SAFE_TEST_FILES-parametrized tests grew from 32 to 33 entries). Combined coverage measured twice, identically, at 24.16299676341062% (up from 24.138741292664996%). 0 cross-scope duplicate node IDs, 0 skip/xfail beyond the pre-existing 1, full-suite-mixed + post-full-suite isolated re-run stable for all 3 target files. Adds no measurable net time cost. Previous baseline (Phase 7 Quality/Top-Level CI Coverage Expansion, 2026-07-27) was combined_pct=24.14 -- kept in _history for continuity, not reused as the active floor. Earlier baselines: Phase 6 Communication/Behavior/Mobile combined_pct=23.45; Critical Operational Expansion combined_pct=23.39; CI Coverage Scope Policy Closure (services-only) combined_pct=23.27; Campaign 1B (2026-07-24) combined_pct=18.85 -- see previous_baseline below for the immediately preceding one.

repeatability.note: Two independent full runs of the new combined command (both steps) produced an identical measurement (deterministic given no test randomization is in use): lines 28932/102467, branches 2946/29462 in both runs. The recorded combined_pct is the true measured value, consistent with lines_covered/lines_valid/branches_covered/branches_valid (see tests/quality/test_bys360_coverage_ratchet.py::test_committed_baseline_counts_are_internally_consistent); the sole safety margin is the pre-existing tolerance_pct field below, unchanged at 0.5 points.

tolerance_rationale: Absorbs float rounding and Windows-worktree-vs-Ubuntu-CI-runner platform noise (this baseline was measured on Windows; the actual CI runner is ubuntu-latest, which can take slightly different code paths on OS-conditional branches). Not intended to absorb a real coverage regression, which is expected to be much larger than 0.5 points in practice.
